sections.heading: arena-palette — Are.na colour palette tool
sections.body:
A local single-file HTML tool (no build step, no server) for fetching images from Are.na channels, extracting colour palettes with tints/shades and semantic colours, and exporting in multiple formats. Currently at v1.23+.

### Sub-areas
- **Core extraction pipeline** — Color Thief v3 (MMCQ) with optional OKLCh clustering; semantic palette via `getSwatchesSync`; proportional colour bar with 1 % floor
- **Text exports** — hex / RGB+HSL / CSS custom properties / Simple Color Palette JSON, all including shared image+source header
- **PNG export renderers** — Bars 2 (reference card) and Dots 1 (dot grid overlay), built as standalone canvas harnesses then integrated; multi-pass downscale blur for background
- **OKLCh pipeline** — in progress; agreed to keep OKLCh through all internal stages and convert only at output; library choice between culori CDN and hand-rolled conversion
- **Colour naming** — color.pizza API integration (`requestedHex` map-key fix; `block.description` object bug fix)
- **UI and accessibility** — three-column layout; mid-grey neutral ground; WCAG AA audit; collapsible channels; CUBE CSS / Atomic Design
- **Public deployment** — localStorage token storage confirmed safe; CORS canvas taint from `images.are.na` CDN needs live testing
- **Build system** — Python concat script (`build.py`); no npm; version comments in file headers
- **Colour algorithm research** — reverse-engineered OKpalette / Adobe Color / Supereasy / Coolors for comparison; Adobe's mood-weighted energy-minimisation approach flagged for potential adoption
- **Swatch file exports** — ASE, GPL and Procreate `.palette` exports added (May 2026); Apple CLR judged infeasible in-browser and deferred
- **Colour ordering and grouping** — `palette_sort.py`: OKLCh hue / lightness / nearest-neighbour orderings; hue-family, band, k-means and near-duplicate groupings; hex and swatch output
todos: Confirm where the OKLCh pipeline got to (planned April) and finish it end to end, deciding between culori and hand-rolled conversion
Test the new ASE, GPL and Procreate exports in Adobe, GIMP and Procreate, and decide how to produce Apple CLR (native helper or script)
Deploy to GitHub Pages and test PNG export CORS behaviour from a real public origin

sections.heading: [[dezoomify]] Alfred workflow
sections.body:
An [[Alfred]] workflow for downloading high-resolution tiled images from museum and gallery websites using dezoomify-rs (installed via Homebrew). Core files: `dezoomify_save.py` (v1.1), `get_browser_info.js`, `test_dezoomify_workflow.zsh`.

### Sub-areas
- **Core workflow** — JXA browser info extraction; Python script with Alfred env vars; temp-file handling using `alfred_workflow_cache`; `sips` for image dimensions; v1.1
- **Site compatibility testing** — flat table of sites with CLI / Alfred / test URL / notes columns; working: National Gallery London / AIC / Wellcome; in progress: Rijksmuseum; failing: NGV / Met / SMK / Van Gogh Museum / V&A / Tate
- **Scraper fallback** — planned Python fallback for sites dezoomify-rs cannot auto-detect (Micrio / Zoomify / IIIF manifest / DZI patterns); Rijksmuseum is priority test case
- **YAML custom dezoomers** — investigated as an alternative to the Python scraper for sites with stable tile URL patterns
- **GitHub issue reports** — drafted IIIF v2 manifest parsing bug report for dezoomify-rs upstream (AIC site: `sc:Manifest` type not handled, wrong image extracted)
- **README and documentation** — rewritten to Alfred Gallery style guide; README.md / README-GALLERY.md / alfred-workflow-setup.md / LICENCE produced
- **Notifications** — diagnosed macOS notification permissions issue (not a script problem)
- **Alfred workflow for Are.na posting** — scoped separately: grab page text + images and post to Are.na with citation metadata; image-picker UX is main challenge
- **UFDC investigation** — University of Florida Digital Collections is a React/OpenSeadragon app; flat JPEGs cap at 1920px, but a tiled IIPImage DeepZoom path exists for full resolution (Sept 2026)
todos: Build the Python scraper fallback for sites dezoomify-rs cannot auto-detect, starting with Rijksmuseum (Micrio) and NGV (Zoomify), as designed in the handoff
Submit the drafted IIIF v2 manifest bug report to dezoomify-rs upstream

A Python script in `md-tools` repo that authenticates via OAuth, downloads favourites and gallery images at best available size, and saves structured JSON metadata with full citation fields.

- **Script** — OAuth via `~/.flickr/`; deduplication across favourites + gallery; best-size selection capped at ~3K; `accessed_url` / `src_url` / `date_accessed` naming conventions
- **Citation metadata** — `citation_markdown` and TASL fields; HTML preserved in description with `description_format: "html"`; location data from `flickr.photos.getInfo`; `date_created_granularity` / `date_created_note` fields
- **Known issue** — TASL format currently collapses Title and Source rather than maintaining the four-part Title/Author/Source/Licence structure
- **Git hygiene** — API keys were committed to history; resolved using `git filter-repo --replace-text` before public push; keys revoked and regenerated
- **Supporting files** — README.md / TODO.taskpaper / CONTEXT.md / .gitignore produced
- **Gallery downloader** — `flickr_gallery_download.py` built in May 2026 as part of a modular pipeline (extract, transform to canonical JSON sidecar, load); 'small pieces loosely joined'
- **Eagle import** — `eagle_import.py` imports image + sidecar pairs into Eagle via its local web API (June 2026)
todos: Fix the TASL citation to the correct four-part Title / Author / Source / Licence structure
Run `eagle_import.py` and the gallery downloader end to end on a real library and record the sidecar-to-Eagle field mapping

sections.heading: Structured data audit and browser plugin (image attribution)
sections.body:
An investigation into whether institution web pages carry enough structured data (JSON-LD / Open Graph / Dublin Core / microdata) to auto-generate image citations. Concluded that no institution provides a complete citation from markup alone; a per-site parser approach is needed.

### Sub-areas
- **Audit** — 11 institutions analysed (AIC / Google Arts & Culture / Art UK / British Museum / Christie's / Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia / Harvard / Met / Royal Academy / Tate); handoff doc saved as `structured-data-audit-handoff.md`
- **Key findings** — `schema.org/VisualArtwork` unused in practice; Dublin Core absent everywhere; Wikimedia Commons is the only well-compliant source; AIC has rich HTML Microdata but no JSON-LD; British Museum `dt/dd` definition list is most complete gallery record
- **Browser plugin scoping** — per-site parser architecture with API fallbacks for Met / AIC / Harvard (all have public APIs); Wikidata reconciliation as cross-site enrichment
- **Artsy API migration** — investigated Artsy API (being retired) as a source of artist identifiers; Wikidata QIDs via P2042 confirmed as best hub
- **Knowledgebase structure** — agreed: markdown files cross-referenced with JSON; Wikidata QID as the linking identifier
- **Commons citation prototype** — `wiki-cite` Safari bookmarklet (Oct 2026) reads MediaWiki imageinfo, Commons Structured Data and Wikidata; outputs YAML, TASL, Harvard-style Markdown, an Eagle list and JSON
- **JSON-LD grounding** — `@context` / `@id` / `@type` concepts related to Kim's canonical sidecar schema and Obsidian frontmatter (Aug 2026)
- **Schema derivation** — TypeScript schema derived from simonw's museums YAML as a model for a small-museums dataset (Sept 2026)
todos: Decide where the per-site parsers live (`md-tools` or a new repo) and define the parser interface; see the Safari clipper section
Reuse `wiki-cite` as the Wikimedia Commons shim, then add Met, AIC and Harvard API shims
Define the artist markdown file structure and write a small Wikidata reconciliation script

sections.heading: Ebook and PDF library organisation (`md-pkim-library`)
sections.body:
Organisation, metadata extraction, and classification of a ~8500-file ebook/PDF library on a mounted file server (`/Volumes/BearsShared/Books`).

### Sub-areas
- **Folder schema** — 13-topic classification with 3 utility folders (`_collections` / `_inbox` / `_purchased-ebooks-backup`); `make-folders.zsh` and `books.txt` definition file produced
- **Metadata extraction** — `extract_book_metadata.py` scans PDFs/EPUBs; outputs to Excel with duplicate flagging (ISBN / filename / fuzzy title+author); `sanitise_for_xlsx()` fix for illegal XML characters
- **Classification CSV** — sample batches with confidence ratings (high/medium/low); ~20–30 % of files have opaque filenames (hashes / DOI strings) needing upstream rename
- **Markitdown batch conversion** — Python script to bulk-convert PDFs/Word docs to markdown; scanned-PDF detection and skip-with-log; `--recurse` flag
- **Tag ontology** — five prefixes shared across Pinboard / Are.na / Eagle / Calibre: `@` people/orgs, `#` topics, `col:`, `project:`, `class:`
- **Duplicate detection** — SHA256-based script keeping the oldest copy, moving others to `/duplicates`, with dry-run reporting (Sept 2026)
- **Status check** — Sept 2026 review of `md-pkim-library` state: ~8,500 files at `/Volumes/BearsShared/Books`
- **Opaque filenames** — file-type and encoding identification for extensionless or UUID-named files
- **Folder creation** — shell patterns (file, stdin, heredoc) for creating the schema folders
todos: Use the metadata spreadsheet with Claude for Excel to improve title guessing (filenames beat first-page text)
Write an upstream rename script for opaque filenames (DOI resolution, ExifTool) before resuming CSV classification
Create the folder structure on the file server with `make-folders.zsh` (if not already done), then dry-run the duplicate finder before migrating files

sections.heading: Obsidian vault management and frontmatter clean-up

sections.heading: dt-knowledge-base — drawing knowledge base
sections.body:

sections.heading: Safari clipper — universal web ingest
sections.body:
An idea for one Safari extension that consolidates dezoomify, citation grabbing, metadata sniffing, batch image download and multi-destination saving, prototyped so far as the `wiki-cite` bookmarklet.

### Sub-areas
- **Concept** — dezoomify IIIF images, auto-citation, schema.org / JSON-LD / Open Graph extraction, best-guess fallbacks, batch select-and-download, routing to Are.na, Markdown + images, Pinboard; YAML or JSON sidecars
- **Port feasibility** — SocialSnag via `safari-web-extension-converter`; missing `chrome.downloads` is the blocker
- **Prototype** — `wiki-cite` bookmarklet in `md - pkim and tools/wiki-cite/`
- **Parser inputs** — structured-data audit findings and tiled-image detection (section 2)
todos: Decide the architecture (Safari Web Extension vs extending the bookmarklet) and list a first-release feature set, citation and metadata first
Extend `wiki-cite` to the Met, AIC and Harvard APIs as the first per-site parsers

sections.heading: Titler (Python) — Markdown link titler

sections.heading: Shared tag ontology and classification
sections.body:
The overarching vocabulary (prefixes, topics, folders, properties) meant to span Finder, Pinboard, Are.na, Eagle, Calibre and Obsidian; home repo `md-pkim-classification`.

### Sub-areas
- **Tag prefixes** — `@` people and organisations, `#` topics, `col:` collections, `project:`, `class:`
- **Folder schema** — 13 topic folders plus 3 utility folders, two levels maximum, tiebreaker rules
- **Evidence** — Pinboard tag-combination analysis; Obsidian tag clustering and property inventory
- **Authority and linked data** — Wikidata as hub, Getty ULAN, JSON-LD concepts
- **Colour vocabulary** — hex ordering and grouping; colour naming (color.pizza)
todos: Reconcile the Obsidian property inventory and Pinboard tag clusters into one controlled vocabulary in `md-pkim-classification`
Publish it as a machine-readable file (YAML or JSON-LD) that each tool can import
Map Eagle, Are.na and Calibre tags to the prefixes and write a conversion script
